hypothesis: Strict signed/unsigned relational scalar reductions with an affine control and an invariant endpoint start+step*span can be split when ordinary relational SCEV trip formulas are unavailable or too conservative. A small equality-witness proof preserves start/end correlation and works for ascending, descending and wrapping controls, including enclosing-loop reuse. This is a legality/storage proof extension before ordinary LV, with independently selected stage VFs and no profitability, pressure, depth, reduction-count or original-vectorizability requirement.
semantics: The existing induction recognition, unique exiting latch, acyclic branch CFG, simplify-form, dedicated exits, LCSSA, reduction-use/feedback, participation, live-out, call/effect, alias and strict/constrained-FP checks remain. Normalize only the analysis predicate for branch polarity; require its continuation predicate to be strict SLT/SGT/ULT/UGT, so equality exits irrespective of operand order. For the admitted integer affine IV {S,+,K}, subtract S from the invariant comparison operand. Recover span only from the identical constant SCEV factor K (or the unit-stride identity); there is no integer division, modular solver, search or inferred nowrap requirement. If the latch compares the backedge value, witness=span-1; if it compares the current IV, witness=span. Evaluate the actual compared addrec at this witness and require its modular difference from the original endpoint to fold to zero. Thus, on every defined execution that reaches that ordinal, the actual original branch exits there. Earlier exits, including those caused by signed/unsigned wrapping order, are allowed: N<=witness+1, never N=witness+1 by assumption. Apply only LLVM existing loop-entry guards to the witness, range-bound it, widen before adding one, and require the completed count to fit uint64 and the original IV type. Take the smaller of this unconditional bound and the existing ordinary count proof. The unchanged checked byte/alignment multiplication and signed alloca-pointer-index ceiling prove every scratch access and counter cast. A private ordinal stores at 0<=i<N<=M and its nuw increment exports actual N through LCSSA. The unchanged consumer performs exactly N ordered updates. Compact participation retains its separate counter, original participation paths/order, P<=N bound and P=0 guard; no fabricated zero contribution is added. All producer arithmetic, flags, comparison operands, branch polarity, guards and operations remain in their original blocks; only the exiting edge is redirected as before. Contributions are computed once without rereads or speculation. Ordered FP updates are cloned with original flags/operand order; the explicit fission FP-reordering option adds no relaxation on this scalar path. Enclosing rows retain their real carries, final stores and future-input aliases, reusing entry-allocated scratch after each consumer. Executable validation is requested against untouched original IR and independent C formulas after one and two ordinary LV invocations. Four new modular relational functions use independent unsigned-C control counting (signed order via sign-bit xor) and require earlier-than-witness exits, full-capacity executions, exact producer/header/latch/consumer counts and nonzero vector/tail visits for every comparison class. Their checker cannot substitute n for the completed count. All original affine, compact, acyclic, canonical and VPlan execution assertions are retained.
costs: No new runtime instructions relative to t000019: the change only proves finite storage bounds; existing private ordinal/completed and compact counters and consumer remain unchanged. Relative to canonical pre-affine splitting, a noncanonical producer has one ordinal PHI, one nuw add per original iteration and one completed-count export; the consumer has a zero-based PHI/add/equality branch. Compaction has one increment per participant, latch merges/count export and the existing empty guard, without a second full-trip ordinal. For maximum M, actual N and compact P, scratch is M times the sum of unique contribution allocation sizes plus ABI padding, statically allocated in function entry even on a bypass, capped at the unchanged default 65536 bytes per candidate and signed pointer-index ceiling. Each mixed affine fixture shares three arrays across four reductions: 65*i32 + 65*double + 65*float = 1044 accounted bytes including 4 padding bytes; logical stores and loads are each 16*N bytes, or 16*P for compaction. The enclosing loop reuses 784 accounted bytes (65*i32 + 65*double plus padding), with 12*N stores and 12*N loads per row, without multiplying capacity by rows. Scalar boundary executions reserve 4/1020/65536 bytes for 1/255/16384 i32 contributions and transfer 8*N logical bytes total (131072 at full capacity); new relational analogues execute capacities 255 and 16384 too. There are no original-input rereads, duplicated producer operations, contribution recomputation, mask arrays, new guards, alias/SCEV versioning, dynamic allocation or unbounded storage. Compile-time additions are a direct predicate/factor scan, a few standard SCEV algebra queries, one affine evaluateAtIteration equality check and the existing bounded guard-rewrite/range machinery. Scratch planning arithmetic was extracted verbatim into one shared helper to diagnose the original scratch rejection without a second implementation. Analysis remarks record the ordinary count/admission outcome separately from the new witness; when remarks are enabled this also computes the old scratch plan for diagnostic purposes. Existing O(B+E) CFG admission and scans/DT recalculation remain. No general proof engine or profitability model was introduced. Test additions and retained failure stdin/commands affect validation only. Physical traffic, stack layout, register pressure, RVV execution and performance are unmeasured.
limitations: The worker did not build LLVM, run any compiler (including a host compiler), execute lit, VectorizeTests, the execution checker, try.sh or target code. Read-only source/diff/log inspection, fixture generation and whitespace review are not fresh validation. The frozen t000019 failure log contains neither missed remarks nor printed SCEVs, so its exact per-function bound/scratch rejection is not claimed observed: the new mandatory diagnostic RUN and ScalarFissionBound remarks are requested to determine and retain it. No callable live harness diagnostic interface was available to the worker; compiler diagnostics are requested only through this report and lit RUNs. The new proof intentionally covers a syntactically recoverable constant SCEV factor and strict continuation comparisons that exit on equality; non-strict continuation, an unreachable equality lattice, a missing unconditional span bound, count overflow or scratch overflow gets no exemption. The ordinary proof remains available for other already-supported shapes. A different but equivalent factorization may remain unproved. This does not broaden arbitrary/pointer/FP inductions, extra recurrences, early exits, internal cycles, unsupported live-outs, independent participation streams, side effects, unsafe calls or strictfp/constrained FP. Scratch remains untiled, full-trip and capped per loop rather than per function. Host fixed-vscale scalar-remainder execution and RVV machine-verified EVL/code generation are separate evidence; neither is RVV target execution or measured speedup. No new corpus selection, direction maturity or speedup is claimed. Benchmarks, harness, other/common worktrees, binaries and Git index/history/refs were not modified; unfinished d2 work was not integrated.
